newsitem.title: USA: UPS sees adverse financial impact from strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS sees adverse financial impact from strike.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc. expects its revenues and earnings to be adversely affected during the first national strike in the company's history, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday.

UPS, the world's largest parcel delivery company, said in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it may lose some customer accounts as a result. But it added that it "cannot predict the financial impact" of the three-day-old strike by 185,000 Teamster members.
"The labour action has already caused a significant loss in volume," UPS said in the filing.

But the company maintained that its current assets and available credit would be adequate to support its operations during the strike. It also said it expects its employee expenses to increase after a new labour agreement with the striking workers is negotiated and ratified.

The company said in the filing that it intends to limit its service during the strike to packages currently in the UPS system and high-priority packages including domestic air express packages and international packages. Where possible, critical and emergency goods will get priority, it said.
